children: Australian equities rose 37 points or 0.4% to 8,769 in early Tuesday trade, snapping two sessions of muted moves as Wall Street’s overnight rally lifted sentiment amid softer oil prices and easing U.S. Treasury yields.
Optimism was also supported by prospects of Middle East talks at the UN and upcoming U.S.–China meetings, though geopolitical tensions lingered.
Gains were broad-based, led by tech, consumer durables, non-energy minerals, and consumer services.
However, upside was capped by inflation worries after Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock struck a hawkish tone in parliament last week, keeping rate-hike risks alive.
Separately, Australia’s four major banks now expect the central bank to raise rates next week, citing energy-driven inflation pressures.
Standout movers included Wisetech Global (3.8%), Xero Ltd. (3.6%), Lynas Rare Earths (2.0%), and REA Group (1.6%).
Investors now turn their focus to the flash September PMI and August labor data for further policy cues.

title: Australian Shares Rebound as Tech Leads
